verdict.rationale: Codex is fundamentally an agentic, natural-language coding tool: users interact via prompts in CLI, IDE, web, and desktop apps to explore code, plan changes, edit files, run commands, and delegate tasks, all driven by NL instructions rather than rigid commands. Extensive first-party docs describe interactive NL sessions, image-based prompts, subagent delegation, and non-interactive NL-driven exec workflows; community evidence corroborates real-world agentic usage (completing complex coding tasks from prompts), though some users report inconsistent agentic quality. Missing for 10: independent benchmarking specifically on NL-command robustness/consistency, and some community reports note agentic reasoning gaps (e.g., 'no idea how to call agents').
